LOS ANGELES, California (CNN)  -- One of two doctors charged with conspiring to furnish drugs to Anna Nicole Smith before her fatal overdose in 2007 surrendered to authorities and was jailed Monday, authorities said. Anna Nicole Smith's boyfriend Howard K. Stern was among those charged last week. Dr. Khristine Eroshevich surrendered at the Van Nuys, California, jail, said police and jail officials. Bail was set at $20,000, but Eroshevich had not posted bail as of Monday afternoon. Eroshevich was charged last week along with Howard K. Stern, Smith's longtime partner and attorney; and Dr. Sandeep Kapoor. Stern and Kapoor were arrested and released from a Los Angeles County jail Thursday night after each posted a $20,000 bond. All three are charged with eight felonies, including conspiring to furnish controlled substances, unlawfully prescribing a controlled substance and obtaining fraudulent prescriptions from June 2004 through January 2007, only weeks before Smith's death. Kapoor and Eroshevich were also charged with obtaining a prescription for opiates by "fraud, deceit or misrepresentation." And each was charged with one count of obtaining a prescription for opiates by giving a false name or address, prosecutors said. "Anna was the center of a cruel tabloid feeding frenzy," Eroshevich's attorney, Adam Braun, told CNN in a statement Monday. "In the face of this, Dr. Eroshevich did her best to help the patient while protecting what little privacy Anna had left. Any actions were done with the patient's well-being in mind and were certainly not criminal." California Attorney General Jerry Brown said the doctors and Stern devised a plan to use fake names so Smith could be prescribed "thousands of pills." The former Playboy playmate and reality TV star was drugged "almost to the point of stupefaction," Brown said. "The quantity of the drugs, the variety of the drugs, the combination at any given point, and her continuing to use that -- that, to a professional, is clear evidence of addiction," Brown said Friday. "These cocktails of methadone and antidepressants and sleeping pills and Xanax, you put all that into a cocktail, it explodes and can cause death, injury and permanent morbidity and disability." Brown said Stern was the "principal enabler" in a conspiracy with two doctors for giving the "known addict" thousands of prescription pills. Stern's attorney Krista Barth said on CNN's "Larry King Live" on Friday night that she thought Brown's comments were prejudicial. "I don't think that this was something that should have been stated in a public forum," Barth said. "I think it's contrary to the rules of professional conduct regarding trial publicity. And you have to wonder why such a statement was made." Smith, 39, was pronounced dead February 8, 2007, after being found unconscious in her hotel room at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino near Hollywood, Florida. A coroner said she died from an accidental overdose of prescription drugs. Officials said that both prescription and over-the-counter drugs were found in Smith's system, including three antidepressant or anti-anxiety drugs. Human growth hormone and chloral hydrate, a sleep medication, were also found in toxicology tests, officials said. CNN's Marc Balinsky contributed to this report.

## Geography and Climate

Located in Southern California, Los Angeles enjoys a Mediterranean climate characterized by warm, dry summers and mild, wet winters. The city stretches across a vast basin bordered by mountains and the Pacific Ocean, giving residents access to both beautiful beaches and scenic hiking trails within the same day.

## Entertainment Industry

Perhaps most famous for Hollywood, Los Angeles has been the heart of the American film and television industry for over a century. The iconic Hollywood sign, major studios like Warner Bros, Universal, and Paramount, and countless celebrities call this city home. The entertainment industry has shaped not only the local economy but also global popular culture.

## Cultural Diversity

Los Angeles is renowned for its incredible cultural diversity, with communities representing nearly every nation on Earth. This diversity is reflected in the city's culinary scene, festivals, and neighborhoods—from Koreatown to Little Tokyo, from Boyle Heights to Thai Town.

## Economic Significance

Beyond entertainment, Los Angeles boasts a diverse economy including technology, fashion, international trade, and tourism. The Port of Los Angeles is one of the busiest shipping ports in the nation, connecting California to global markets.

## Conclusion

Los Angeles, California continues to attract dreamers, entrepreneurs, and visitors from around the world, cementing its status as a global city that blends creativity, diversity, and opportunity in a uniquely Californian setting.

# Howard K. Stern, Two Doctors Charged in Anna Nicole Smith Drug Case

**LOS ANGELES** — California prosecutors have filed criminal charges against Howard K. Stern, the longtime companion and attorney of the late Anna Nicole Smith, along with two physicians, alleging they conspired to provide the former Playboy model with excessive quantities of prescription drugs, including controlled substances, in the years before her 2007 death.

## The Charges

Stern, along with psychiatrist Khristine Eroshevich and Smith's personal physician Sandeep Kapoor, faces multiple felony counts related to conspiracy to possess controlled substances by fraud and administering excessive quantities of drugs to a known addict. Prosecutors allege the defendants used aliases and false names on prescriptions to conceal Smith's drug dependency and provide her with a steady supply of sedatives, opioids, and anti-anxiety medications.

According to the criminal complaint, the prescriptions were allegedly written under names other than Smith's own in an effort to obscure the volume of medication she was receiving and to prevent scrutiny from pharmacies and regulatory agencies.

## Toxicology Findings

Smith, 39, was found dead on February 8, 2007, in a hotel room in Hollywood, Florida. The Broward County medical examiner ruled her death an accident caused by "combined drug intoxication."

The toxicology report identified nine different drugs in her system at the time of death, including:

- **Chloral hydrate** — a powerful sedative-hypnotic, found at levels described by the medical examiner as consistent with chronic use
- **Benzodiazepines**, including clonazepam (Klonopin), diazepam (Valium), and alprazolam-related compounds
- **Diphenhydramine** — an over-the-counter antihistamine with sedative properties
- Additional prescription sedatives and muscle relaxants

The medical examiner concluded that no single drug caused Smith's death, but rather the cumulative depressive effect of multiple sedatives acting on her central nervous system, compounded by an ongoing case of the flu and a bacterial infection.

## Prosecutorial Allegations

Prosecutors allege that Stern was aware of Smith's long-standing struggles with substance dependency, dating back to before the death of her son, Daniel Smith, who died of a similar combined drug intoxication just months before his mother's passing. Despite this, the complaint alleges, Stern facilitated continued access to controlled substances rather than seeking intervention.

Dr. Eroshevich is accused of writing prescriptions in the names of Stern and another associate to disguise the true recipient of the medications. Dr. Kapoor faces similar allegations regarding excessive prescribing practices.

## Defense Response

Attorneys for all three defendants have denied wrongdoing, characterizing the prescriptions as legitimate medical treatment for documented conditions, including chronic pain and anxiety. They argue that Smith was under the ongoing care of multiple physicians and that no single doctor could have known the full extent of her combined medication use.

## Legal Proceedings

If convicted, the defendants face potential prison time, though the specific charges primarily carry the possibility of fines and probation rather than lengthy incarceration. The case has drawn significant media attention given Smith's celebrity status and the parallel tragedy of her son's death.

Formal arraignment proceedings are expected in the coming weeks, with both prosecution and defense teams indicating the case may take months to resolve given its complexity and volume of medical evidence.

*This case remains under active adjudication, and specific details may be subject to court rulings on evidence and admissibility.*

*(CNN) —* A second physician charged in connection with the 2007 death of former Playboy model and reality TV star Anna Nicole Smith turned himself in to authorities Tuesday, posting bail hours after prosecutors unsealed charges accusing him of overprescribing medication to the celebrity in the months before she died.

The doctor, whose identity was confirmed by the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office, surrendered at a downtown booking facility shortly before noon and was released after posting bond set by a superior court judge. He did not comment to reporters gathered outside but was photographed entering a waiting vehicle with his attorney.

The surrender comes roughly a week after a companion physician tied to the case turned herself in on similar charges, part of a broader indictment that also named Smith's longtime partner and attorney, Howard K. Stern.

**Charges Stem From Yearslong Investigation**

According to court documents, prosecutors allege the doctor conspired with others to furnish excessive quantities of controlled substances — including sedatives and opioid painkillers — to Smith using aliases to conceal the volume of drugs being prescribed. Investigators say the practice continued even as Smith's physical and psychological health visibly deteriorated in the months leading up to her February 2007 death in a Florida hotel room, which a medical examiner attributed to an accidental overdose of prescription drugs.

The California attorney general's office, which took over the case after a grand jury declined to file charges in 2007, said the renewed investigation uncovered evidence that the defendants "conspired to feed the addictions of an addicted person" rather than treat legitimate medical conditions.

**Defense Pushes Back**

Attorneys for the doctor rejected the allegations firmly outside the courthouse.

"My client is an accomplished physician who treated Ms. Smith with the same care and professional judgment he has shown thousands of patients over his career," the attorney said in a statement to reporters. "These charges rely on hindsight and speculation, not medical fact. We intend to fight this vigorously and expect full vindication at trial."

"This was not medicine. This was enabling," a spokesperson for the attorney general's office said following the arraignment of the first doctor last week. "The law applies to physicians just as it does to anyone else who knowingly contributes to a fatal addiction."

**Case Details and What's Next**

Both doctors face multiple felony counts, including conspiracy to furnish controlled substances to an addict and prescribing under a false name. If convicted, they could face several years in state prison, though legal analysts say sentencing in such cases often hinges on plea negotiations.

Stern, who was also charged in the same indictment, has denied wrongdoing through his attorney and is expected to enter a plea at a future hearing.

A pretrial conference for all three defendants has been scheduled in Los Angeles Superior Court in the coming weeks. Attorneys on both sides indicated they expect the case to draw continued media attention given Smith's celebrity status and the unresolved questions surrounding her final months.

CNN's legal affairs unit will continue to follow developments in the case.
